summary_plain: Moves about 18 arcseconds per hour across 24 images over 44.1 hours. Not yet checked against JPL's catalog of known asteroids and comets.

source.processing_note: Zodiacal light model (ZODI) and residual background (2-D plus per-row) subtracted; pixels SPHEREx flags as unusable, and detector-edge rows with raised noise from edge glow, are filled from their neighbors (or set to the sky level) for display only and only inside the detector, while measurements use the masked data; pixels outside the detector are transparent; fixed asinh stretch shared by all images of the field; 64 x 64 px stamp at 6.15 arcsec/px centered on the detection

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 185 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.not_checked_reason: JPL Horizons did not answer for 774 Armor (A913 YE), the closest known object (about 85″ away in JPL's quick search).

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

anomaly.reason_plain: About 1.4× farther from the Sun than the median of the objects we have tracked
anomaly.definition: Isolation Forest over motion rate, motion across the ecliptic, ecliptic latitude, distance from the Sun and infrared colour of every published object with a motion fit over 3 or more detections (not two-detection pairs or likely artifacts). It ranks how unlike the others an object is; unusual does not mean new or unexplained.

history.change: linked 24 detections over 4 visits from 2025-09-19 to 2025-09-21

disclaimer: An unmatched candidate may be an imaging artifact, a measurement error, or an object missing from the catalogs we checked. This is not a discovery claim.
